items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: You look at people like Monk, Charlie Parker, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Louis Armstrong, Billie Holiday. When you look at these people, they have one thing in common and that is they were all original.

ctx.x: And you think that the record companies don’t encourage the individuality.

No I think the record companies encourage musicians who sound like other musicians, musicians who are going back ten, twenty, thirty years, and trying to play like the people who invented and created that music at that time and sort of regurgitated, you know, almost like a repertory concept. And as opposed to the industry encouraging and signing and promoting original thinking musicians and artists to try to take the music further. You know we’ve always looked forward. You think of the greats, let’s talk about…
